ENT Clinical Note  

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and suspected trigger/exposure:
  • 3-day history of loose, watery diarrhea and intermittent left-sided lower-abdominal cramping.  
  • Possible foodborne trigger: Chinese takeaway consumed 4 days ago.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset ≈3 days ago.  
  • Frequency of stools: 6–7/day.  
  • Initial vomiting (now resolved).  
  • Felt febrile at onset; currently afebrile by history.  
  • Ongoing weakness and shakiness; appetite decreased but tolerating liquids.

- ENT symptoms:
  • No throat swelling/closure sensation, no voice change/hoarseness, no dysphagia/odynophagia, no drooling.  
  • No nasal or ocular symptoms.  
  • No stridor, noisy breathing, or dyspnea.  
  • No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling.  
  • No ear pain/hearing change.  
  • No neck pain or swelling.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar episodes reported.  
  • No prior hospital or emergency visits for this issue.

- Allergies: Not discussed / not documented.

- Current medications:
  • Asthma inhaler (type/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • No other regular medications.  
  • Paracetamol suggested (dose/route/frequency not documented) for fever/aches.

- Social context:
  • Lives with wife and two children.  
  • Working as an accountant; has remained at work despite symptoms.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported.  
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, wheeze, or respiratory distress reported.  
- Mental status: Alert; reports weakness but no syncope.  
- Vitals: Not recorded.  
- Examination findings: None performed/documented.  
- Others present: Not applicable (remote consult).

Assessment:
- Acute self-limiting gastroenteritis, likely foodborne; no evidence of ENT involvement or airway compromise at this time.

Plan:
- Conservative management: oral hydration, oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte), light diet.  
- Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol for fever/discomfort (two tablets up to four times daily as advised).  
- Rest: Advised 2–3 days off work.  
- Escalation/red-flag advice: seek medical review if unable to keep fluids down, persistent fever, blood in stool or vomit, increasing abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or no improvement within 3–4 days.  
- Follow-up: Reassessment if symptoms persist >3–4 days; consider stool studies and further evaluation.  
- Avoid suspected trigger foods until recovery.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected: allergies list, detailed asthma medication name/dose, vital signs, physical exam (including ENT and abdominal).  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.
